ecological dynamics and complex adapted functions. Evochora asks a complementary question: how do the fundamental rules of a world shape the evolutionary outcomes within it?\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo answer this, the physics of the world are themselves the experiment. Thermodynamic models, mutation operators, resource distribution, and death mechanics are all swappable plugins. Instead of asking \"what evolves under these rules?\", researchers can ask \"how do the rules shape what evolves?\" — and test the answer by changing them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor the full scientific motivation, see the \u003ca href=\"/evochora/evochora/blob/main/docs/SCIENTIFIC_OVERVIEW.md\"\u003eScientific Overview\u003c/a\u003e. spatial assembly language. The default primordial organism (\u003ca href=\"/evochora/evochora/blob/main/assembly/primordial/main.evo\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eassembly/primordial/main.evo\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e) is a conservative replicator: a main loop checks the energy level and decides whether to call the reproduction or energy harvesting subroutine. It is enclosed in a STRUCTURE shell but does not overwrite other organisms.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis design leaves room for experimentation. For example:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAggressive variant\u003c/strong\u003e — overwrite neighboring organisms' code to claim territory\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDefensive variant\u003c/strong\u003e — add a subroutine that periodically repairs the STRUCTURE shell against aggressive neighbors\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCooperative variant\u003c/strong\u003e — write data molecules into the environment as signals; other organisms can read them to coordinate behavior or share energy\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEfficient variant\u003c/strong\u003e — optimize the energy harvesting routine to cover more ground with fewer instructions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo create your own organism:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEdit or create a new mutation operators that run during organism reproduction. Built-in plugins: gene insertion, substitution, deletion, and duplication.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEnvironment plugins\u003c/strong\u003e — Implement \u003ccode\u003eITickPlugin\u003c/code\u003e to add new environmental processes. Built-in plugins: solar radiation, geysers, and seed energy distribution.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDeath handlers\u003c/strong\u003e — Implement \u003ccode\u003eIDeathHandler\u003c/code\u003e to control what happens when an organism dies (e.g., decay into energy).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAnalytics plugins\u003c/strong\u003e — Extend \u003ccode\u003eAbstractAnalyticsPlugin\u003c/code\u003e to define custom metrics exported as Parquet. Built-in plugins: population metrics, vital stats, age distribution, genome diversity, and more.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCompiler extensions\u003c/strong\u003e — Each compiler phase is extensible via handler registries (directives, IR converters, layout, linking, emission).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eVM instructions\u003c/strong\u003e — Add new implements the simulation environment and its physical laws. It provides the n-dimensional grid in which organisms exist as spatially distributed code, subject to thermodynamic constraints. Each organism is an independent virtual machine with its own registers, stacks, and pointers. Organisms interact with the world exclusively through their Instruction Pointer (IP) and Data Pointers (DPs) — they have no global view of the simulation.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThermodynamic costs are fully configurable: actions can cost energy, produce entropy, or both. An organism dies when its energy is depleted or its entropy exceeds its threshold.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUnlike classical von Neumann architectures, jump instructions in Evochora do not target exact addresses. Instead, they resolve targets through fuzzy label matching based on Hamming distance. This makes genomes inherently resilient to mutations that insert, delete, or shift code — a prerequisite for meaningful evolution.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eConceptual Architecture of an Evochora Organism\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-conceptual-architecture-of-an-evochora-organism\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Conceptual Architecture of an Evochora Organism\" href=\"#conceptual-architecture-of-an-evochora-organism\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"         +---------------------------------------------------------------+\n         |                 Evochora \u0026quot;World\u0026quot; The design separates concerns into a frontend (parsing and analysis) and a backend (layout and code generation). Most phases are extensible via handler registries, allowing new syntactical features to be added in a modular way. EvoASM supports procedures, scoped variables, macros, and spatial layout directives for placing code in n-dimensional space.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCompiler Frontend\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-compiler-frontend\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Compiler Frontend\" href=\"#compiler-frontend\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe frontend parses the source code and transforms it into a machine-independent Intermediate Representation (IR).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePreprocessor\u003c/strong\u003e: Handles macros (\u003ccode\u003e#macro\u003c/code\u003e) and file inclusions (\u003ccode\u003e#include\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eParser\u003c/strong\u003e: Converts tokens into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). simulation engine is decoupled from data processing. Raw simulation data flows through a queue into a persistence service, then through indexers into a queryable database. This separation means the simulation can run at full speed while data is processed independently — and raw data can be reindexed at any time with new or modified indexers.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll pipeline services except the simulation engine are designed as idempotent competing consumers. All inter-service communication is abstracted behind resource interfaces (queues, storage, topics, databases). The default mode runs all components in a single process, but this architecture lays the groundwork for horizontal scaling and distributed deployments.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv tick-by-tick view of the simulation. memory access (Fixed)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eRewards for logical tasks (NOT, AND) (Fixed)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eDifferential equations (flow, kernel) (Fixed)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eExtensible via Plugins (Thermodynamics, Resource Distribution)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOrganism Body\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eDisembodied (Code string only)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eDisembodied (CPU + Memory buffer)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eMorphological patterns (solitons)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eIP + DPs navigating spatial grid\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInteraction Model\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eParasitism (reading neighbor's RAM)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eLimited (mostly competition for space)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eCollision, fusion \u0026amp; repulsion of patterns\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eDirect \u0026amp; Spatial (via DPs); Planned: Signaling\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEvolutionary Driver\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eImplicit competition for memory/CPU\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eDirected (user-defined rewards)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eSpontaneous pattern formation\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eMetabolic \u0026amp; spatial constraints\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExecution Model\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eSequential (Single IP)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eSequential (Single IP)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eParallel (Continuous dynamics)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eSequential; Here are some research directions the architecture is built to support:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMutation \u0026amp; Evolvability\u003c/strong\u003e — How do different mutation regimes affect long-term evolutionary potential? Compare gene insertion, substitution, deletion, and duplication strategies or design your own.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThermodynamic Selection\u003c/strong\u003e — How do energy and entropy policies shape population dynamics? Explore the space between harsh and permissive environments.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCooperation \u0026amp; Communication\u003c/strong\u003e — Can organisms that coordinate through environmental signals (molecules placed in the grid) outcompete solitary strategies?\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDigital Chemistry\u003c/strong\u003e — Can reaction chains (A + B → C + Energy) lead to emergent trophic levels and metabolic recycling?\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDigital Eukaryogenesis\u003c/strong\u003e — Can intra-organism parallelism lead to internal division of labor, analogous to the prokaryote-to-eukaryote transition?\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eComplexity Measurement\u003c/strong\u003e — How do you rigorously quantify whether evolution produces increasingly complex organisms? The data pipeline persists complete organism state for external analysis.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOpen-Ended Evolution\u003c/strong\u003e — What conditions help a population overcome the next complexity hurdle? <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What is Evochora?</h2><a id="user-content-what-is-evochora" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What is Evochora?" href="#what-is-evochora"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Evochora is a scientific simulation platform where digital organisms — written in EvoASM, a spatial assembly language — live as distributed code in an n-dimensional grid. They interact with their surroundings exclusively through local pointers and replicate under configurable thermodynamic constraints. There is no fitness function and no external selection pressure.</p>
<p dir="auto">The platform is extensible at every layer: the compiler pipeline, the VM instruction set, the mutation operators, and the rules of the world are all configurable or replaceable through plugins. A decoupled data pipeline persists complete simulation state and exports all metrics as standard Parquet files — ready for analysis in Python, R, Jupyter, or DuckDB. A web-based frontend allows tick-by-tick inspection and debugging of organism behavior.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Evochora?</h2><a id="user-content-why-evochora" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Evochora?" href="#why-evochora"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Landmark platforms like Tierra and Avida demonstrated that digital evolution can produce genuine ecological dynamics and complex adapted functions. Evochora asks a complementary question: how do the fundamental rules of a world shape the evolutionary outcomes within it?</p>
<p dir="auto">To answer this, the physics of the world are themselves the experiment. Thermodynamic models, mutation operators, resource distribution, and death mechanics are all swappable plugins. Instead of asking "what evolves under these rules?", researchers can ask "how do the rules shape what evolves?" — and test the answer by changing them.</p>
<p dir="auto">For the full scientific motivation, see the <a href="/evochora/evochora/blob/main/docs/SCIENTIFIC_OVERVIEW.md">Scientific Overview</a>. For the personal story behind the project, see the <a href="/evochora/evochora/blob/main/docs/ORIGIN_STORY.md">Origin Story</a>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Trust Your Results</h3><a id="user-content-trust-your-results" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Trust Your Results" href="#trust-your-results"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Deterministic Simulation</strong> — Seed-based; identical input produces the identical simulation state and trajectory, guaranteed — independent of thread count and of pause/resume</li>
<li><strong>Complete Data Persistence</strong> — Every tick is recorded; nothing is lost or aggregated away</li>
<li><strong>Decoupled Data Pipeline</strong> — Raw data can be reindexed at any time with new or modified analytics plugins</li>
<li><strong>No Built-In Selection Bias</strong> — By default, no global culling or task-based rewards; organisms survive through their own actions in a spatial environment</li>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Writing Your Own Organisms</h3><a id="user-content-writing-your-own-organisms" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Writing Your Own Organisms" href="#writing-your-own-organisms"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Organisms are programmed in <strong>EvoASM</strong>, Evochora's custom spatial assembly language. The default primordial organism (<a href="/evochora/evochora/blob/main/assembly/primordial/main.evo"><code>assembly/primordial/main.evo</code></a>) is a conservative replicator: a main loop checks the energy level and decides whether to call the reproduction or energy harvesting subroutine. It is enclosed in a STRUCTURE shell but does not overwrite other organisms.</p>
<p dir="auto">This design leaves room for experimentation. For example:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Aggressive variant</strong> — overwrite neighboring organisms' code to claim territory</li>
<li><strong>Defensive variant</strong> — add a subroutine that periodically repairs the STRUCTURE shell against aggressive neighbors</li>
<li><strong>Cooperative variant</strong> — write data molecules into the environment as signals; other organisms can read them to coordinate behavior or share energy</li>
<li><strong>Efficient variant</strong> — optimize the energy harvesting routine to cover more ground with fewer instructions</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">To create your own organism:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Edit or create a <code>.evo</code> file in <code>assembly/</code></li>
<li>Configure it in <code>config/evochora.conf</code> (see <code>simulation-engine.options.organisms</code>)</li>
<li>Run <code>bin/evochora node run</code> — the engine compiles automatically</li>
</ol>

<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Language Reference:</strong> <a href="/evochora/evochora/blob/main/docs/ASSEMBLY_SPEC.md">docs/ASSEMBLY_SPEC.md</a></li>
<li><strong>Syntax Highlighting:</strong> VS Code/Cursor extension in <a href="/evochora/evochora/blob/main/extensions/vscode/README.md"><code>extensions/vscode/</code></a></li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Evochora is extensible at multiple levels through Java plugin interfaces:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Mutation plugins</strong> — Implement <code>IBirthHandler</code> to define new mutation operators that run during organism reproduction. Built-in plugins: gene insertion, substitution, deletion, and duplication.</li>
<li><strong>Environment plugins</strong> — Implement <code>ITickPlugin</code> to add new environmental processes. Built-in plugins: solar radiation, geysers, and seed energy distribution.</li>
<li><strong>Death handlers</strong> — Implement <code>IDeathHandler</code> to control what happens when an organism dies (e.g., decay into energy).</li>
<li><strong>Analytics plugins</strong> — Extend <code>AbstractAnalyticsPlugin</code> to define custom metrics exported as Parquet. Built-in plugins: population metrics, vital stats, age distribution, genome diversity, and more.</li>
<li><strong>Compiler extensions</strong> — Each compiler phase is extensible via handler registries (directives, IR converters, layout, linking, emission).</li>
<li><strong>VM instructions</strong> — Add new instructions to the ISA via the instruction registry.</li>
</ul>
<br>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How It Works</h2><a id="user-content-how-it-works" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How It Works" href="#how-it-works"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Evochora is built as a modular stack of four components: Runtime, Compiler, Data Pipeline, and Web Frontends.
Each layer is independently extensible through plugins and registries.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Runtime</h3><a id="user-content-runtime" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Runtime" href="#runtime"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The runtime implements the simulation environment and its physical laws. It provides the n-dimensional grid in which organisms exist as spatially distributed code, subject to thermodynamic constraints. Each organism is an independent virtual machine with its own registers, stacks, and pointers. Organisms interact with the world exclusively through their Instruction Pointer (IP) and Data Pointers (DPs) — they have no global view of the simulation.</p>
<p dir="auto">Thermodynamic costs are fully configurable: actions can cost energy, produce entropy, or both. An organism dies when its energy is depleted or its entropy exceeds its threshold.</p>
<p dir="auto">Unlike classical von Neumann architectures, jump instructions in Evochora do not target exact addresses. Instead, they resolve targets through fuzzy label matching based on Hamming distance. This makes genomes inherently resilient to mutations that insert, delete, or shift code — a prerequisite for meaningful evolution.</p>
